params.place: on the map: the whole world from space, Antarctica at the bottom

moments.what: the white ice cap of Antarctica glows at the bottom of the world
cracks run across the ice and it starts to drip
meltwater spreads out from the coast in rings
coastlines around the world flicker blue
the camera pushes in on the flickering coasts of Europe and Asia
a question mark drops onto the ocean
the camera eases back to the whole world

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Antarctica's ice melts, all of it. Which countries vanish from the map first?

params.place: on the map: Antarctica from above, the South Pole

moments.what: the camera dives toward the South Pole
Antarctica traces in light
ANTARCTICA writes across the ice
the South Pole pin drops in the middle of the ice
the ice thickens into a dome
a cut line shows the ice deep over the land
mountain peaks show faintly under the ice

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: From space, Antarctica is a whole white continent at the bottom of the world, buried under ice so thick it hides whole mountain ranges.

params.place: on the map: the Southern Ocean and every ocean beyond it

moments.what: the ice cap shrinks, its edge dripping
blue water rings spread out from Antarctica
arrows of water run north into the Atlantic, Indian and Pacific
the camera pulls back over all the oceans
every coastline on the map traces in blue
the sea level line on the map rises
a question mark drops onto the map

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Melt it, and all that water runs into the one ocean that touches every coast on Earth. So where does it hit first?

params.place: on the map: the Netherlands and the North Sea

moments.what: the camera flies to Europe
the Netherlands traces with its flag
windmills stand on the flat land
the North Sea writes on
water pours in over the coast
most of the country turns to sea, the windmills sinking
a pin on Amsterdam sinks under the water
a pin on Rotterdam sinks under the water

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Start in Europe. The Netherlands is low, flat land, and the North Sea pours in until most of it is gone, Amsterdam and Rotterdam included.

params.place: on the map: Bangladesh and the Bay of Bengal

moments.what: a plane flies east over the map
Bangladesh traces with its flag
rivers fan out into the sea
a small boat bobs at the river mouth
the water creeps north over the land
BAY OF BENGAL writes on the new sea
a pin on Dhaka sinks under the water

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Fly east to Bangladesh, a country of river mouths. Most of it slips under the Bay of Bengal, and the capital, Dhaka, goes with it.

params.place: on the map: Florida and the Gulf of Mexico

moments.what: the camera crosses the Atlantic
Florida traces in light
a palm tree and a beach hut stand on the peninsula
the sea eats in from both sides
only a few patches of high ground are left
the palm tree sinks, the water closing over it

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Across the Atlantic, the sea closes in on Florida's long peninsula, and most of the state is under water too.

params.place: on the map: the world, three countries flooded but still there

moments.what: the Netherlands, Bangladesh and Florida pulse on the map
their high ground glows green
small hills rise above the water on each
a question mark spins over the Indian Ocean
the camera pushes toward the open ocean

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: But those three keep their high ground. So which countries lose everything?

params.place: on the map: the Maldives in the Indian Ocean

moments.what: the camera dives into the Indian Ocean
a chain of tiny islands traces in light, MALDIVES writing on
palm trees and little houses stand on the islands
a house stands beside a height marker
the water rises over the islands one by one
the flag sinks below the waves
only rings of ripples are left on the sea

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Out in the Indian Ocean lie the Maldives, hundreds of coral islands, none much higher than a house. Every one goes under. A whole country, gone.

params.place: on the map: Tuvalu and the Marshall Islands in the Pacific

moments.what: the camera swings out over the Pacific
the islands of Tuvalu light up
the Marshall Islands light up further north
both flags plant on their islands
the coral rings glow
an eraser sweeps the islands off the map

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Then the Pacific: Tuvalu and the Marshall Islands, whole nations built on low rings of coral, wiped off the map.

params.place: on the map: the world with its new coastlines, a sea gauge at the Maldives

moments.what: a sea gauge post rises out of the ocean
the water climbs the gauge
the gauge sign lands on the figure
the camera pushes in on the gauge
a tiny island hill stands beside the gauge, far below the line
the camera pulls back over the new world map

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: All because the sea would stand about 58 m higher than it does today, and their highest ground is nowhere near that.

params.place: on the map: back to the whole world from space

moments.what: the Netherlands glows on the map
Florida glows across the ocean
the new coastlines trace in blue
a comment bubble pops
the water drains back off the map
the ice cap of Antarctica returns, white, as in the first frame

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Netherlands or Florida: which new coastline surprised you more? Tell me below, before Antarctica's ice melts, all of it.

disclaimer: Maps simplified. Borders as recognised by the country each video is about.
